questions.text: Place order calls Reserve stock, then Take payment. Is that one synchronous request chain, and who drives the sequence: Order service, or each service triggering the next?
questions.about: Place order -> Reserve stock -> Take payment

questions.text: What does Take payment actually do: call the provider and wait for an answer, or just start a payment? Why is there a separate Payment webhook step after it?
questions.about: Take payment -> Payment webhook

questions.text: What happens to the order and the reservation if the payment fails or the customer never pays within the 10 min?
questions.about: Reservations expire after 10 min

questions.text: What does the Payment webhook tell us, who receives it (which service), and how does it find the matching order?
questions.about: Payment webhook

questions.text: How is a duplicate webhook detected? What is stored, where, and what is the key?
questions.about: Webhooks can be late or duplicated, so dedupe

questions.text: In the late-payment case, who checks whether stock is gone and who does the re-reserve? How does the Order service learn the result?
questions.about: Late payment when the stock is gone: re-reserve, otherwise refund and cancel

questions.text: The diagram shows Confirm order leading to both Clear cart and Refund. When does each branch happen? Is Refund every time?
questions.about: Confirm order -> Refund

questions.text: What are the order statuses, and who stores and changes them? What does 'Cart cleared via event' mean here: who publishes it, who consumes it, and what if it is lost?
questions.about: Order statuses are tracked / Cart cleared via event

answers.text: Not one chain. The Order service drives: it calls Inventory (HTTP), then Payment (HTTP), then waits for a payment event. Orchestration in one place keeps status in one DB and makes the failure branches simple.
Take payment asks the provider to charge and returns at once with the payment recorded as PENDING. The real result comes later by webhook because it can take up to 30 minutes.

Declined: Order marks PAYMENT_DECLINED, releases the hold, leaves the cart untouched. Hold lapses before payment: stock returns to sale; if payment later succeeds, the claim step tries a fresh re-reserve, else refund and cancel. No webhook ever: unknown, listed as an open question.

It reports succeeded or declined for a charge. The Payment service receives it, matches it to the order through the order id / provider reference stored in its payment record, then publishes an event carrying the order id.
Payment stores the provider's event id in its own DB with a unique constraint. A webhook whose id is already stored is ignored with an OK reply.

Order, on PaymentSucceeded, asks Inventory to claim the hold. Inventory checks it and, if lapsed, tries the re-reserve; it returns claimed or out-of-stock in the HTTP reply, so Order learns the result directly. Re-reserve is kept from the original note; it is a small addition and avoids refunding when stock is still available.
The diagram was wrong. Confirm leads only to Clear cart. Refund happens only on the late-success, stock-gone branch, which cancels the order instead of confirming it. Diagram redrawn.

Statuses are listed in the document and only Order stores and changes them. Order publishes OrderConfirmed, Cart consumes it and clears the cart. Events go through a table in the publisher's DB and are resent until accepted, so a lost event is re-sent and repeats are harmless.

questions.text: If the HTTP call to Inventory times out or errors, or Order crashes right after reserving, what state is the order in and what happens next? Is the call retried, and could a hold be left behind?
questions.about: Order asks Inventory to reserve all lines for 10 min (HTTP)

questions.text: If the charge request to Payment fails or times out, what does Order do? Does the order stay AWAITING_PAYMENT, and what does the customer see while waiting for the webhook?
questions.about: Order asks Payment to charge (HTTP, order id as idempotency key)

questions.text: How does the Order service receive PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined: does it subscribe to the broker, and what does it do if it is down or the event arrives twice?
questions.about: Payment stores event id, updates payment record, publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined with order id

questions.text: If the claim call to Inventory fails or times out after payment succeeded, what happens? Could the customer be charged with the order stuck, and how is a repeated claim for the same order handled?
questions.about: Order asks Inventory to claim the hold (HTTP)

questions.text: When the customer retries after a decline, is it the same order or a new order with a new id? How does this affect the idempotency key and the reservation?
questions.about: Order = PAYMENT_DECLINED, asks Inventory to release the hold

questions.text: If the customer presses Place order twice, or the cart changes while an order is in progress, what prevents two orders or two charges?
questions.about: Customer presses Place order

answers.text: Order saves AWAITING_STOCK first, then retries the reserve call a few times (about one minute) with the same order id; Inventory keeps one hold per order id, so a retry returns the existing hold. If no answer ever comes, Order sets FAILED_TECHNICAL, asks Inventory to release, and the customer retries. A hold left by a crash expires after 10 minutes anyway, so none is stuck. Chosen as the simplest handling with no new mechanism beyond retry and one status.

Order retries the charge with the same order id; the key makes it safe. If Payment never answers, Order sets FAILED_TECHNICAL and releases the hold. While waiting for the webhook the order is AWAITING_PAYMENT and the customer sees Processing payment. If a charge went through anyway, the webhook triggers an automatic refund because the order is no longer AWAITING_PAYMENT.

Yes, Order subscribes to the broker. If it is down, the broker holds the events until it returns. A repeated event is harmless because Order acts only when the order is AWAITING_PAYMENT. Exact broker redelivery settings are not specified.

Order retries the claim until Inventory replies and alerts a person if it keeps failing. The customer has been charged and the order waits in AWAITING_PAYMENT meanwhile, but the payment is recorded so nothing is lost. A repeated claim for the same order returns claimed, since Inventory keeps one hold per order id. Alert destination is unknown and listed as open.

A retry is a new order with a new order id, so a new idempotency key and a new reservation. The declined order released its hold. Reusing the old id would make the provider return the declined charge, so a new id is required.

A database rule allows one open order per cart; a second press returns the existing order, so one order and one charge. Cart edits after Place order do not affect the order because it uses its snapshot. Side effect: confirmation clears the whole cart, which may drop later additions; listed as open, not decided.

questions.text: If Order crashes after saving AWAITING_STOCK but before (or while) calling Inventory, what restarts the sequence? Who notices an order stuck in AWAITING_STOCK?
questions.about: Order service saves order AWAITING_STOCK

questions.text: How does the customer's screen learn the result (Processing payment, then confirmed, declined, cancelled)? Does the client poll Order, or is something pushed to it?
questions.about: Customer sees Processing payment

questions.text: While an order sits in AWAITING_PAYMENT (up to 30 min, or forever if no webhook), Place order just returns that same order. Can the customer do anything else with that cart in that time, such as start a fresh order?
questions.about: A database rule allows only one open order per cart

questions.text: Order asks Payment to charge using the snapshot. Does Payment get the amount and customer payment details in that request, or look them up somewhere? Where does the amount come from?
questions.about: Order asks Payment to charge

questions.text: Who consumes RefundRequested and how does it find the payment to refund? Does the order status change when the refund finishes or fails?
questions.about: Order = CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, publishes RefundRequested

answers.text: Nothing restarted it, which was a real hole: such an order would block the cart. Now Order, on start and then every minute, finds orders in AWAITING_STOCK for over two minutes and repeats the reserve call with the same order id, which is safe. The two minute and one minute figures are placeholders, listed as open.
The client polls Order for the order status; nothing is pushed. Polling is the simplest option and needs no new mechanism. Poll interval is not decided and listed as open.

No. While an order is open (up to 30 minutes, or longer if no webhook comes), Place order returns that same order and no new one can start for the cart. This follows from the one-open-order rule. If no webhook ever arrives the cart stays blocked; that is the existing open question about querying the provider or cancelling.

Order sends Payment the order id and the amount, the sum of the snapshot lines, so the amount comes from the snapshot and Payment looks nothing up. How the customer's payment method details reach the provider is not decided and is listed as an open question. Raw card details are not stored in any of our services in this plan.

Payment consumes RefundRequested. It finds the payment record by the order id in the event and creates a refund record, then refunds at the provider. The order status does not change when the refund finishes or fails; the refund record in Payment holds that state, and a failing refund retries and alerts a person. Order stays CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, or whatever status it had when the late success arrived.

questions.text: If Order crashes after Inventory replies 'all reserved' but before the charge call is made, what state is the order in and what restarts it? The crash sweep only mentions AWAITING_STOCK.
questions.about: Order asks Payment to charge (HTTP, retried, order id as idempotency key) / Order = AWAITING_PAYMENT

questions.text: If Order crashes while retrying the claim after PaymentSucceeded, does the broker redeliver the event? At what point does Order tell the broker it has handled the event, and what does Order do with the redelivered event if the status is still AWAITING_PAYMENT?
questions.about: Order receives event: is order AWAITING_PAYMENT? / Order asks Inventory to claim the hold

questions.text: If the release call to Inventory also fails, or Order itself crashes before sending it, what happens to the hold? Is the release retried, or do we just wait for the 10 minute expiry?
questions.about: Order = FAILED_TECHNICAL, asks Inventory to release

questions.text: If Payment crashes or the provider call fails after Payment received the charge request, what does the payment record look like and what does Order get back? Could a webhook arrive for a charge Payment has no record of?
questions.about: Payment calls provider, stores payment record PENDING, returns at once

questions.text: How does Payment match the webhook to a payment record: by provider reference, or by order id? And what happens if the webhook reports a result for an order id that Payment cannot find?
questions.about: Provider webhook arrives at Payment, possibly 30 min later

answers.text: Two cases. If Order crashes after Inventory replied but before saving AWAITING_PAYMENT, the status is still AWAITING_STOCK, so the crash sweep repeats the reserve (returns the existing hold) and goes on to charge. If it crashes after saving AWAITING_PAYMENT but before the charge reply, the sweep now also finds AWAITING_PAYMENT orders older than two minutes whose charge is not marked accepted and repeats the charge call, which is safe because of the order id key. A small 'charge accepted' mark is stored in Order for this. Chosen because otherwise the order would block the cart; Order cannot read Payment's DB, so it needs its own mark.

Yes, the broker redelivers. Order acknowledges the event only after it has finished handling it (claim reply received and status saved). If it crashes mid-claim the event comes again, the order is still AWAITING_PAYMENT, so Order repeats the claim, which is safe because Inventory keeps one hold per order id. Exact broker redelivery settings are not decided and are now listed as open.

Release is best effort, tried once and not retried. If it fails or Order crashes first, the hold simply expires after 10 minutes and the stock goes back on sale. Chosen because the expiry already is the safety net, so a retry mechanism adds nothing. Cost: stock stays unavailable up to 10 minutes.

Payment saves the payment record as PENDING before it calls the provider. If the provider call fails, Payment returns an error; if Payment crashes, Order gets no answer. Either way Order retries with the same order id, the provider's idempotency key stops a second charge, and Payment returns the existing record. Because the record is saved first, a webhook for a charge Payment has no record of should not happen in normal operation; if it does, see Q24.

By order id. Payment sends the order id to the provider as the charge reference and looks up the payment record by the order id in the webhook, because the provider reference may not be stored yet if Payment crashed after the provider call. If no record is found, Payment stores the event id, alerts a person, replies OK and publishes nothing, since it cannot tell which order the money belongs to. It is not verified that our provider lets us set a reference and echoes it back in the webhook; that is added as an open question.

teachbacks.text:
1. Place order. The customer presses Place order. The Order service takes a snapshot (cart lines and prices copied from the cart) and saves a new order as AWAITING_STOCK. A new order id is made each press. The Order DB holds this state. Before saving, Order checks whether this cart already has an open order (AWAITING_STOCK or AWAITING_PAYMENT). If it does, Order returns that order, so a double press gives one order and one charge. A database rule also allows only one open order per cart. If Order crashes, the sweep (step 8) picks the order up later. The customer's screen polls Order for the status.

2. Reserve. Order calls Inventory over HTTP to reserve all the snapshot lines for 10 minutes. The order id is the idempotency key. Inventory keeps one hold per order id, so a retry returns the existing hold. The hold and its expiry are stored in the Inventory DB.
   - If any line is short, nothing is reserved (the reserve is all-or-nothing). No payment is requested. Order sets REJECTED_SHORT_STOCK and tells the customer which items are short. The cart is unchanged.
   - If Inventory gives no answer after a few retries (about one minute in all), Order sets FAILED_TECHNICAL, tries once to ask Inventory to release the hold, and tells the customer to try again. The cart is unchanged.
   - If all lines are reserved, go to step 3.

3. Charge request. Order sets AWAITING_PAYMENT, and the customer sees "Processing payment". Order then calls Payment over HTTP with the order id and the amount (the sum of the snapshot lines). The order id is the idempotency key, and the call is retried on error or no answer. Payment does not look anything up. It first stores a payment record as PENDING, keyed by the order id. Then it calls the provider with the order id as both idempotency key and charge reference. Then it replies to Order, and Order marks the charge as accepted. If the provider call fails or Payment crashes, Order gets an error or no answer and retries. The key stops a second charge, and Payment returns the existing record. If the retries run out, Order sets FAILED_TECHNICAL and tries once to release the hold.

4. Waiting for the provider. Order now waits. Nothing in the main flow moves until the provider's webhook reaches Payment. It usually takes seconds but can take up to 30 minutes.

5. Webhook. The provider calls Payment over HTTP with a result (succeeded or declined) and an event id.
   - If the provider event id is already in the Payment DB, Payment ignores it and replies OK.
   - Otherwise Payment finds the payment record by the order id in the webhook. If there is no record, it stores the event id, alerts a person, replies OK and publishes nothing.
   - If a record is found, Payment stores the event id (unique constraint), updates the payment record, and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined with the order id. The event is written to Payment's outbox table in the same transaction as the change, and a sender repeats it to the broker until the broker accepts it.

6. Order handles the payment event. Order subscribes to the broker. It acts only if the order is AWAITING_PAYMENT, so a repeated event does nothing. Order acknowledges the event only after it has finished. If Order crashes mid-handling, the broker redelivers the event and the order is still AWAITING_PAYMENT. If Order is down, the broker holds the events.
   - Declined: Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and tries once to release the hold. The cart is unchanged, and the customer can retry as a brand new order with a new id, charge key and hold.
   - Not AWAITING_PAYMENT (for example FAILED_TECHNICAL, where a charge went through after Order gave up): on success Order publishes RefundRequested (via its outbox) and the status stays as it is. A decline is ignored.
   - Succeeded while AWAITING_PAYMENT: go to step 7.

7. Claim. Order calls Inventory over HTTP to claim the hold, retried until Inventory replies. If it keeps failing, a person is alerted. The payment is already recorded, so nothing is lost meanwhile. Inventory checks the hold:
   - If the hold is live, it is claimed. A repeated claim of an already claimed hold returns claimed.
   - If the hold lapsed, Inventory tries one all-or-nothing re-reserve of every line.
   - Claimed, or lapsed but all lines re-reserved: Order sets CONFIRMED and publishes OrderConfirmed. Cart consumes OrderConfirmed and clears the whole cart. Clearing an empty cart is harmless. The screen's polling then shows confirmed.
   - Lapsed and stock gone: Order sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, publishes RefundRequested and emails the customer. The order is never partially shipped.

8. Crash sweep. When Order starts, and then every minute, it looks for stuck orders. An order in AWAITING_STOCK for over two minutes gets the reserve call repeated, then the charge. An order in AWAITING_PAYMENT for over two minutes whose charge is not marked accepted gets the charge call repeated. Both are safe because of the order id as the idempotency key. Without the sweep such an order would block the cart for good.

9. Refund. Payment consumes RefundRequested. It finds the payment record by the order id, creates a refund record, and refunds the full amount at the provider. If the provider fails, the refund stays PENDING and is retried until it succeeds. Repeated failure alerts a person. On success the refund is DONE. The order status does not change when the refund finishes or fails. The refund record in the Payment DB holds that state.

Failures that leave the cart alone: any failure before CONFIRMED leaves the cart exactly as it was. If a release fails, or Order crashes before releasing, it is not retried. The hold expires after 10 minutes and the stock goes back on sale. Lost or repeated events are handled by the outbox resending until the broker accepts, and consumers ignoring repeats.
gaps: The document says the screen polls Order for status, but not how the screen's request reaches Order, so I cannot say how the Place order press itself arrives at Order.

When Order's no-answer retries on Inventory or Payment run out and FAILED_TECHNICAL is set, I am not told exactly what the customer sees for a technical failure beyond 'try again'. The screen status list only names Processing payment, confirmed, declined and cancelled.
The document does not say what happens if no webhook arrives within 30 minutes. The order stays AWAITING_PAYMENT and the cart is blocked, and the document lists this as undecided.
The document does not say how the customer's payment method reaches the provider, so I cannot explain what the provider charges against.
The document does not say where the alerts go, the retry interval for refunds and claims, or which service sends the cancellation email. Order only triggers it.

The document does not say how Order gets the hold-release or re-reserve outcome for a lapsed hold beyond the reply to the claim call. It does not say how Order tells 'stock gone' from 'claimed' in the reply.
The document does not say what the sweep does to an AWAITING_STOCK order after the reserve is repeated if the reserve is short (I assume the normal step 2 outcomes apply, but this is not stated).

The document does not say what keeps a hold alive during a long wait for the webhook, since a hold lasts only 10 minutes and the webhook can take 30. It only says that a lapsed hold is re-reserved at claim time.
